housing: Rushmoor is made up of the twin towns of Aldershot and Farnborough, both shaped by the army and aviation. Older terraces sit near the town centres and the former military areas, with large post-war estates around them and big new developments such as Wellesley on former army land. Around one in five households rents privately, a share that grew between 2011 and 2021. Many rented homes are flats in converted terraces and newer apartment blocks near the stations.
checkinTips: New-build homes at Wellesley: photograph snagging items, sealant around baths and any marks on fresh paintwork, as these get disputed.
Apartment blocks near Aldershot and Farnborough stations: note fob, key and parking permit counts, and the bin and bike store access.
Victorian terraces in Aldershot and North Camp: photograph sash or replacement windows, chimney breasts and any damp in rear rooms.
Flats over shops in the town centres: record the condition of the street door, stairs, smoke alarms and any noise or smell from the shop below.
Post-war estate houses in Cove and North Town: photograph fences, sheds, garages and the condition of the garden, as these are often in the inventory.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Rushmoor Borough Council's Private Sector Housing Team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
